# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is a modern, applied introduction to **machine vision** for undergraduate engineering students. It covers the complete pipeline — image formation, classical image processing, learning-based recognition, 3D vision, motion, and modern foundation models — through reproducible Python and Google Colab laboratories.

## How this book is organized

The book follows a 14-week course and is divided into four parts:

- **Part I — Foundations:** what machine vision is, image representation, image formation and calibration, and multi-scale data structures.
- **Part II — Classical Processing:** preprocessing, filtering and morphology, segmentation, and features/matching.
- **Part III — Learning-Based Vision:** object detection (two-stage and one-stage) and deep segmentation.
- **Part IV — 3D, Motion and Frontiers:** 3D vision, motion and tracking, and vision-language models.

Each chapter contains learning outcomes, worked examples, a **linked Colab lab**, a common-misconceptions box, exercises, and further reading.

## How to use this book

::: {.callout-tip}
## Students
Read the chapter, then open the linked Colab notebook and complete the exercise and challenge. The `Q&A` sections are for self-testing.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Instructors
Each chapter maps to the course learning outcomes. A companion question bank and slide decks are maintained in the teaching repository.
:::

## Conventions

- **Notation** is defined on first use and summarized in the appendix.
- **Code** is Python (OpenCV, NumPy, Matplotlib, PyTorch, Ultralytics).
- **Colour figures** use a colour-blind-safe palette.
